about: A made-up real-estate brokerage for the retrieval benchmark: the kind of operating knowledge a brokerage's agents would share, written as explicit memories. Every company, tool and process here is invented. Following the never-store policy (docs/never-store.md), it holds no people's names, no addresses, no contact details and no money figures. Questions mix plain paraphrases, partial word overlaps with distractor memories, and graph questions that name a process and expect the memory about the vendor or tool it depends on. Written once and never used to tune a retriever: if a result looks wrong, write a new set rather than change this one.

memories.content: The listing launch checklist covers professional photos, MLS entry and the yard sign before a home goes live.
New listings get professional photos from Brightframe Studio before they go live.
Brightframe Studio also shoots drone video when the listing agent asks for it.
A new listing is entered in the MLS within one business day of the signed listing agreement.
Showing feedback is requested from the buyer's agent the morning after each showing.
Website leads go to the next agent on the lead rotation, and the rotation resets every Monday.
Every new lead gets a first reply within fifteen minutes during business hours.
Open houses run on Saturday and Sunday afternoons, with visitor sign-in on the tablet kiosk.
A file is ready for closing review only when the inspection report, the disclosure packet and the appraisal are attached.
Home inspections are booked through Keystone Inspections, who send their reports within two days.
Contacts and follow-ups live in Harborline CRM, and every client call is logged there the same day.
Harborline CRM sends a reminder before each past client's birthday so the agent can send a card.
After twenty-one days on market without an offer, the listing agent gets a pricing review.
The transaction coordinator handles every pending sale from signed contract to closing day.
The listing presentation deck is in the shared drive under Marketing.
Every agent completes fair housing training once a year.
Yard signs are ordered from Northpoint Signs and go up the day a listing is live.
All flyers, postcards and social posts use the brokerage's approved templates.
Transaction files are kept for seven years after closing.
The office copier is serviced every other month.
The weekly team meeting is on Tuesday mornings.
Agents park in the back lot during open houses so visitors can use the front.
The break room fridge is cleaned out on Friday afternoons.
New agents shadow a senior agent at two showings before running their own.
The office closes early on the day before a holiday.
